intro: Hey everyone — I'm Maya Chen. I work as a music data analyst for a streaming platform — basically, I'm the person who helps decide what shows up on your Release Radar and Discover Weekly. Every day I look at numbers like energy, danceability, and genre, and I ask: what does the data say about what you'll love? Today you'll do the same thing — and you'll learn that probability isn't just a formula in a textbook. It's how Spotify knows what to play next.
act1Post: Look at that. 600 songs, sorted by energy. Pop is all over the place — some mellow, some intense. Edm clusters at the high end. Rap spans the whole range. Every genre has a fingerprint in these numbers. And once you see it, you can't unsee it. That's what data does: it shows you patterns your ears already knew but couldn't name.
act2Start: Here's where it gets interesting. Pick a feature — energy or danceability — and slide the threshold. What counts as 'high'? Watch how the fraction changes per genre. Some genres are predictable — you already know which one owns the high-energy zone. But the numbers will surprise you on others.
act2Genre: Now pick a genre. Once you do, look at two numbers: given this genre, how many songs are high energy? And given high energy, how many songs are this genre? Same songs. Same threshold. Different questions. Watch how the two probabilities tell a different story.
act2Compare: Two probabilities. Same threshold. Same data. Different question. P(high energy | genre) asks: 'if I play this genre, what are the odds it's intense?' P(genre | high energy) asks: 'if a song is intense, what are the odds it's this genre?' I use both of these every week building playlists. One tells me about the genre. The other tells me about the whole catalog. Most people mix them up — and that's exactly what your chapter is teaching you to see.
act3Top: You just did what I do at work every day. You picked a feature, set a threshold, and compared two conditional probabilities. The math is just counting — but knowing *which* count to use for *which* question? That's the skill. And it's the same skill doctors use reading a test result, and the same one we use deciding what song to play you next.
act3Closing: So next time Spotify recommends a song and it fits — or doesn't — you'll know why. A model looked at the numbers and calculated a probability. Not a guarantee. A probability. Just like what you did here. Different data, same math.
act3Game: Before we look at the answer, let me test your ear. I'll show you a song's energy and danceability scores — you tell me the genre. This is exactly the kind of thing our playlist models do: look at the numbers and make a prediction. Let's see how your guesses compare to the conditional probabilities you just calculated.
